items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: He’s using AI to screen existing compounds for therapeutic potential | University of Pittsburgh
items.summary: Developing pharmaceuticals using AI isn’t new, but it is laborious and often leads to a dead end. “If you generate a brand-new molecule, that’s actually a limitation,” Wang said. “A lot of compounds can’t be synthesized, and that is a big issue.” [...] This back and forth is the GAN’s training. Over time, the generator learns to generate fingerprints that more closely resemble those of real molecules. Researchers then search chemical databases for existing compounds with similar footprints; the AI-generated pattern leads to the discovery of real molecules that researchers can test — no need to synthesize a new molecule. [...] In a paper published Oct. 28 in the journal Science Advances, Wang outlined Full-Spectrum Generative Lead Discovery (FSGLD), a novel, practical and reusable framework that takes advantage of generative AI to screen for existing compounds with potential for therapeutic development.

items.title: Có Nên Học Công Nghệ Thông Tin? Học CNTT Có Khó Không?
items.summary:
## Ai Phù Hợp Với Ngành Công Nghệ Thông Tin?

Ngành Công nghệ thông tin phù hợp với người yêu thích công nghệ, có tư duy logic, kiên trì giải quyết vấn đề và sẵn sàng tự học. Không nhất thiết phải biết lập trình trước khi vào đại học, nhưng học sinh nên có hứng thú tìm hiểu cách các hệ thống máy tính và ứng dụng hoạt động.

### Những Tố Chất Phù Hợp Với Ngành CNTT

Dưới đy là một số đặc điểm có thể giúp học sinh học tập và phát triển trong ngành. [...] Có nên học Công nghệ thông tin? Học CNTT có khó không? Đy là những băn khoăn phổ biến của học sinh THPT khi đứng trước lựa chọn ngành học. Công nghệ thông tin (CNTT) vẫn có nhiều hướng nghề nghiệp trong lĩnh vực phần mềm, dữ liệu, bảo mật và hệ thống máy tính. Tuy nhiên, ngành học này đòi hỏi khả năng tư duy logic, kiên trì thực hành và chủ động cập nhật kiến thức. Để quyết định có nên học CNTT, học sinh cần nhìn nhận thực tế thị trường việc làm, độ khó của chương trình và mức độ phù hợp với [...] Nên học Công nghệ thông tin nếu bạn yêu thích công nghệ, có khả năng tư duy logic và sẵn sàng dành thời gian học tập, thực hành lu dài. Ngành CNTT phù hợp với người muốn sử dụng máy tính và phần mềm để giải quyết vấn đề thực tế, không chỉ với những học sinh đã biết lập trình từ THPT.

Tuy nhiên, quyết định chọn ngành cần dựa trên sở thích, năng lực và mục tiêu nghề nghiệp thay vì kỳ vọng rằng học CNTT chắc chắn có thu nhập cao.

### Những Lý Do Nên Cn Nhắc Ngành Công Nghệ Thông Tin

I still don't understand why everyone is not using this yet. Thanks to it, a year ago I increased my income to 15,000 dollars a month

Andrey Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI, published a simple idea that got 25 million views: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

You point Claude Code to a folder, drop any source in there (an article, transcript, PDF) and Claude reads it, links it, and saves it into a living wiki of everything you know. It compounds like interest: the more you feed it, the smarter it gets

Here is the gist:

Paste the file with Karpathy's wiki idea and tell Claude to build it

Claude creates three folders: raw for sources, wiki for its pages, CLAUDE
which runs everything

Drop any source into raw and say ingest this

Ask questions across everything, forever

5 minutes to set up, and you never start with an empty chat again

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary:
So, what—or who—will keep us safe from AI? Looking to regain some faith in humanity, I called a theologian who often meets with the AI labs. If there’s even a slim chance that we’re losing control of the essential institutions that undergird society, he said, then we should focus on foiling that. But AI raises other questions too. What does it mean to be conscious? To create? To commune with other people? The answers are “entirely up for grabs,” he said. My anxiety’s still kicking around, but I [...] Most members of the panel were skeptical about any pause in development: They nearly all agreed that, with big AI companies so tightly cuffed to the trains of capitalism, a pause wouldn’t last long. “Democracy” and “governance” came up often—or anti-democracy, as more than one person suggested that AI’s current trajectory is tyrannical. Lawmakers have a big role to play, but many of my sources think governments will be too slow; one prominent technologist said it’s almost absurd to view the US [...] MOST OVERBLOWN RISK: Runaway intelligence  
There’s this broad, general notion that AI systems getting smarter is a risk in and of itself, as opposed to the many specific risks we need to worry about. I don’t buy into the notion that overall improvement in AI has an inevitable downstream harm. It’s better to first specify what downstream risks you’re worried about, because the defenses you come up with will be different.

Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more.
